newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ASEAN mulls setting up regional energy centre.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN mulls setting up regional energy centre.

text.p: Senior energy officials of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) are considering setting up a regional energy centre by January 1999, a top Philippine energy official said on Tuesday.

"Based on the talking points to be discussed by senior officials with their energy ministers and President (Fidel) Ramos tomorrow, the ASEAN energy centre may be set up by January 1, 1999," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Details of the plan were not disclosed.
The Philippines is hosting a three-day annual meeting of senior officials and energy ministers which began on Monday.
Energy ministers are expected to adopt the resolutions hammered out by the senior officials on July 2.

"I am confident that through the ASEAN spirit of solidarity and cooperation, we shall be able to agree on the structural and developmental reforms to bring into the mainstream of our endeavors, the ASEAN energy centre," Philippine Energy Minister Francisco Viray said in a speech to be delivered at the meeting on Wednesday.

In last year's meeting, senior energy officials agreed to transform the existing ASEAN-EC Energy Management Training and Research Centre (AEEMTRC) project into a more permanent institution, the ASEAN centre.
The AEEMTRC, which earlier had aimed to conduct studies on natural gas development in the region, has relied on the European Commission for funding.
Aside from the energy centre, Viray said an "ASEAN energy freeway" composed of a regional gas pipeline and an ASEAN power grid must be coordinated with similar projects with new ASEAN members.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. It has recently agreed to admit Cambodia, Laos and Burma.
